extracted.intended_audience: Frontiers peer reviewers, handling editors, editors, and submitting authors
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher-level guidance describing Frontiers' peer review model, manuscript acceptance criteria (the VALID standards), permitted review workflows (independent + interactive), reviewer/editor responsibilities, and grounds for rejection. Targeted at reviewers, editors and authors participating in Frontiers' peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality-based acceptance model
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers employs a quality-based acceptance model rather than rejection-rate targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "We don't reject manuscripts based on their perceived potential impact, nor do we set a rejection rate." Acceptance should be driven by whether manuscripts meet quality standards, not by quota or impact expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision-making roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Three key decision-makers in the process: handling editors recommend rejection, editors decide acceptance, and chief editors handle acceptance/rejection determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies responsibilities and escalation path for manuscript decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid research question and hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five VALID manuscript acceptance standards: research question and hypothesis must be valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the acronym VALID that defines required standards for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate, transparent methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five VALID manuscript acceptance standards: methods must be appropriate and transparently reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess methodological suitability and transparency (e.g., reproducibility, clear description of methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language clarity and presentation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five VALID manuscript acceptance standards: manuscript must meet language clarity and presentation standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability, clarity of expression, and adherence to presentation conventions; poor language can be a ground for rejection or revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with editorial and ethical policies
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five VALID manuscript acceptance standards: the submission must be in line with editorial and ethical policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes compliance with declared policies on ethics, conflicts, data sharing, consent, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Driven by adequate literature review
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five VALID manuscript acceptance standards: the work should be driven by an adequate literature review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether prior work is sufficiently cited and the manuscript situates itself within the existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid research question (rejection ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be rejected for having an invalid research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should identify when the central research question lacks grounding, relevance, or coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological errors (rejection ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be rejected for methodological errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes inappropriate design, major flaws in experimental/statistical approach, or lack of reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of originality or plagiarism (rejection ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be rejected for lack of originality or plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty and check for unoriginal content or unattributed reuse of others' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient language quality (rejection ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be rejected for insufficient language quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor English or presentation that prevents understanding can be a cause for rejection or mandatory revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical violations (rejection ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be rejected for ethical violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes issues like lack of ethical approval, data fabrication, or other breaches of research ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship policy breaches (rejection ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be rejected for breaches of authorship policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes inappropriate attribution, ghost authorship, or disputes over author contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biased references (rejection ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be rejected for biased references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether references are unfairly selective or omit important contrary literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misleading conclusions (rejection ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be rejected for drawing misleading conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether conclusions are supported by the data and analyses presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudoscientific inquiry (rejection ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be rejected if they constitute pseudoscientific inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject work that lacks scientific rigor or is not grounded in accepted scientific methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review phase
rubrics_metrics.description: For most article types, reviewers first assess manuscripts independently using standardized templates within ten days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full reviews involve a separate independent assessment stage; reviewers should complete thorough individual evaluations and use provided templates; ten-day target for initial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive review phase
rubrics_metrics.description: After independent review, authors and reviewers engage in real-time forum discussions to address concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive stage is used to clarify comments, negotiate revisions, and allow direct dialogue between authors and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short review workflow for certain article types
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorials and Classifications (short reviews) proceed directly to the interactive phase and may involve only the handling editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain article types bypass the independent-review stage; handling editor may perform the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer/editor expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must possess relevant expertise to review/handle the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers should have subject-matter competence appropriate to the manuscript's topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must maintain objectivity in their assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid personal bias, conflicts of interest, and ensure impartial evaluation of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete thorough assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must complete thorough assessments of manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed, constructive evaluations covering methods, data, interpretation, and literature context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must respond promptly during the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely completion of reviews and engagement in interactive stages is required; independent-review target is ten days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behave professionally
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must behave professionally in communications and reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courteous, respectful tone in critiques and interactions; unprofessional behavior may lead to removal from assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid coercive citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must avoid coercive citation practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not request citations for the sake of inflating metrics or for unrelated self-citation; such behavior is prohibited and may result in removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for non-adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants who do not adhere to established standards will be removed from their assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance with expertise, objectivity, timeliness, professionalism, or anti-coercion policies can result in removal from review/editor duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-anonymized review model
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers operates a single anonymized model: reviewers know who the authors are, but reviewer identities are anonymous unless reviewers choose acknowledgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer anonymity is preserved by default; reviewers may opt to be acknowledged on publication.
